newsitem.title: USA: Insured loss from U.S. snowstorm put at $110 mln.
newsitem.headline: Insured loss from U.S. snowstorm put at $110 mln.

text.p: A snowstorm that struck the northeastern United States on March 31 and April 1 caused an estimated $110 million in insured damage, an industry trade group said on Wednesday.
Property Claim Services, an industry-supported group that tracks insurance losses, said seven states from Pennsylvania to Massachusetts were affected by the heavy, wet snow and strong winds.

The storm buried parts of the Northeast in as much as three feet of snow, downing power lines and trees and bringing transportation to a halt. In addition to Pennsylvania and Massachusetts, parts of New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island and New Hampshire were affected.
Severe weather in the northern plains and central region of the United States this week is likely to result in additional insured losses, PCS senior claim consultant Jim Welsh said.
A blizzard dumped up to three feet of snow on parts of the northern plains on Sunday, resulting in flooding and widespread power outages.
Much of the central United States experienced more snow and cold early Wednesday and a second blast of cold was forecast for Thursday and Friday.
Welsh said an estimate of the insured damage from the Midwest's severe weather is likely sometime next week.
